reason: E1 directly supports that oxidation induces hierarchical heterogeneities and enhances hardness in group IV-V RMPEAs, but it does not provide evidence that these heterogeneities act as a diffusion barrier, reduce oxidation rate, or delay crack initiation. The cited evidence therefore supports the formation and hardness premises but leaves the mechanistic claims about diffusion and cracking unsupported.
premises: Oxygen exposure induces hierarchical heterogeneities (nanoscale interstitial complexes, tertiary phases) in group IV-V RMPEAs
These heterogeneities form a graded microstructural barrier at the oxide-metal interface
This barrier enhances hardness and impedes oxygen diffusion
The barrier reduces oxidation rate and delays crack initiation compared to inert-atmosphere baseline
